marks.gloss_en: ספק נפשות להקל -- Mar Zutra's version is the lenient one, and in doubt of life one is lenient
Mareimar, asked by Ravina which version the halakha follows (Mar Zutra teaches leniently, Rav Ashi stringently): the halakha follows Mar Zutra
כדרב עולא בריה דרב עילאי -- all a sick person's needs are done through a gentile on Shabbat
וכדרב המנונא -- in a matter with no danger, one tells a gentile and he does it
Rav Ulla brei deRav Ilai: all the needs of a sick person are done through a gentile on Shabbat
כי הא דברתיה דרב חסדא -- she immersed within thirty days without her husband, caught cold and died (a maaseh; no support kind exists for one)
Rava: this was said only when her husband is not with her; but when her husband is with her, her husband warms her
מדאתמר: הקיז דם ונצטנן עושין לו מדורה אפילו בתקופת תמוז -- a fire for one who is not a woman in childbirth, in summer
one makes a fire for a woman in childbirth on Shabbat in the rainy season
Abaye to Rabba: והא קעבר מר משום בל תשחית -- in breaking the bench, the master transgressed 'do not destroy'!
בל תשחית דגופאי עדיף לי (= p_bal_tashchit_degufai_adif)
Rabba: the 'do not destroy' of my body is preferable to me
a woman in childbirth, as long as the womb is open, whether she said 'I need' or said 'I do not need' -- one desecrates Shabbat for her
Abaye: [the opening of the womb begins] from when she sits on the birthstool
Abaye: [the opening lasts] three days
within three days, if she says 'I need' -- one desecrates Shabbat for her
for a woman in childbirth -- thirty days
for Shmuel they split a teak chair
a person should always sell the beams of his house and buy shoes for his feet
Rav: [the needs of a meal are] meat
דילמא ... ואתי לידי סכנה -- the pair's own reason (Rav with Shmuel)
one who lets blood should not sit where the wind blows
דאי לא טעים מידי ... -- the pair's own reason (Rav with Shmuel)
one who lets blood should taste something and only then go out
whoever makes light of the meal after bloodletting, Heaven makes light of his sustenance, and they say: he took no pity on his own life, shall I take pity on him?
Shmuel used to let blood in a house of seven bricks and a half [-brick thick]; one day he did so and felt [weak]; he checked, and one half-brick was missing
Shmuel, on the day he let blood, they made him a dish of spleens
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak to the Sages: I beg of you, on the day of bloodletting tell your households 'Nachman has come to visit us'
all artifices are forbidden, except this artifice, which is permitted
Ablat, finding Shmuel lying in the sun: wise man of the Jews, can what is bad become good?
rather, there is a day in the whole year on which the sun is beneficial -- the day on which the Tammuz season falls [and that is why Shmuel lay in the sun]
